title: Optima Filings rule, v1
description: One filing obligation in one jurisdiction. See docs/rule-authoring.md — you can usually copy a neighbouring rule and change three fields.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema. Gives editors autocomplete and inline validation.

id.description: Stable, kebab-case, jurisdiction-prefixed: us-wa-sos-annual-report. A PERMANENT PUBLIC IDENTIFIER — the B2B API and customer integrations key off it. Never rename one; supersede it instead.

jurisdiction.description: US for federal, ISO 3166-2 for states (US-WA), US-WA/seattle for a municipality.

title.description: What the filer sees. 'Annual Report', not the rule id.

agency.description: The body it is filed with, spelled out: 'Washington Secretary of State'.

entityTypes.description: Every legal form this rule applies to. A rule applies if the entity holds ANY of them.

cadence.description: How often it recurs and what the due date is anchored to.

dayOfMonth.description: A day past the end of the month clamps to the last day; it does not roll into the next one.

oneOf.description: Due on the anniversary of formation — month AND day come from the ENTITY, so every entity has a different due date. Oregon (ORS 65.787(1), 60.787(1), 63.787(1): "by the corporation's anniversary"). There is deliberately no dayOfMonth: that is the whole distinction from formation-month, where the RULE names the day. The two agree only when an entity was formed on a month end, which is why picking the wrong one is a silent up-to-30-day error.

amountMinorUnits.description: INTEGER MINOR UNITS. 6000 is $60.00. Never a float — a rounding error in a fee is a support ticket and a credibility hit.

conditions.description: The rule applies only when ALL entries hold. An entry is either a single test, or an {"anyOf": [...]} group that holds when ANY of its members does — for a threshold the statute writes as 'X or Y', such as Form 990's receipts-or-assets test. A condition may only test a fact the entity fact model defines; rules:validate enforces that.

anyOf.description: Holds when any member holds. One level deep only — a group may not contain another group. Nesting would make rules markedly harder for a non-developer to author and for a reviewer to check against a statute, which is the point of the format.

form.description: Form number or name, where the agency uses one.

citation.description: REQUIRED. The statute, regulation, or agency page this came from — 'RCW 24.03A.075'. A rule without a citation is unreviewable. Cite the primary source, never another compliance vendor: they are wrong often enough that copying them imports their errors.

citationUrl.description: Direct link to the statute or agency page, where one exists.

agencyUrl.description: The agency's OWN page for this filing — where a filer goes to file it and to read the current fee, form and deadline. Distinct from citationUrl, which is the legal source a reviewer checks the rule against. Both are needed because the statute frequently does not carry the operative detail: RCW 23.95.255(4) hands the due date to the secretary of state, and 8 Del. C. 502 sets no fee at all. Required in practice for every shipped rule; optional in the schema only because a filing with no agency page on the public web is conceivable.

lastVerified.description: The date a human last read the primary source and confirmed this rule. Bumping it without re-reading is worse than leaving it stale — it converts an honest 'unknown' into a false 'checked'.

status.description: 'draft' means written but NOT yet checked against the primary source by a human. It is the honest state for a rule you are unsure about, not a lesser form of 'active' — contribute a draft rather than asserting something you have not verified. Promotion to 'active' means someone read the statute.

effectiveFrom.description: First date this version of the rule governs.

effectiveTo.description: Last date it governs. Absent means still in force. When a fee or deadline changes, set this and add a NEW rule — never edit in place, or the historical answer is destroyed and the change escapes review.

supersededBy.description: Id of the rule that replaced this one.

weekendRule.description: Opt in only where the statute or agency actually says a weekend deadline moves, and pick the direction the statute states. Rolling by default, or guessing the direction, would invent a legal position the rule never claimed. roll-forward: the IRS moves a weekend due date to the next business day. roll-backward: an agency asking for the last business day OF A PERIOD, such as WAC 434-120-140(2)(a), moves it earlier.

notes.description: Anything a reviewer needs — a quirk, an ambiguity, what was checked.
